title: Lost: The Usual Crate
summary: It happened again. Same hauler line, same captain, same 'settled dust' — except this crate split open over Choir Hollow and scattered five packets of Agricultural Material (the manifest says seeds; the manifest is sweating) across the lamp ring and the temple steps. Sweep every packet before vespers, before the Choir plants them liturgically out of spite.

objectives.label: Slip over the crater rim before the vespers bell
Sweep three packets off the lamp ring — casually, like weather
Lift the last two from the temple steps — do NOT make eye contact with a Cantor
Get the Agricultural Material back to the Guild exchange intact

offer.text: Ash. Remember the crate that fell off a hauler and became your little detective story? Good news: the Guild fixed nothing. Same line, same captain, new crate — and this one burst open over Choir Hollow and scattered five packets of seeds across consecrated geography. I need them swept up before vespers.

The complication: the Choir believes, sincerely, that objects which arrive from the sky are *correspondence*. If a Cantor blesses a packet it becomes, spiritually, mail — and liturgical mail cannot be surrendered without a hearing. I've already lost one pumpkin to due process. There is an heirloom pumpkin growing at the lamp ring that is, legally, a parishioner.
So: steal the mail, dodge the clergy, beat the bell. For the Guild. Quietly.
'Recover prepaid freight from an unscheduled landing.' Words are free, Ash, use the expensive ones.

accept.text: *a hymn, on the open band, pointedly serene* — the Hollow reminds all riders that what the sky entrusts to the ground, the ground answers for. Also, whoever chalked THIS lamp ring full of packet-mud may wish to hurry. For their aura.

That was a threat. A beautiful, legally-actionable threat. Lamp ring first — three packets — then two on the temple steps, and if Brother Decibel is mid-sermon do NOT stop to enjoy it, he's very good and we are very timed.
Copy. Five packets, one bell, zero pumpkins joining the Choir on my watch.

complete.text: Five of five, before vespers, and — I'm counting — zero litigation. Ash Varga, the exchange owes you a fruit basket, which is ironic, and which I am therefore withholding.

We saw the whole thing, courier. Every sweep, every dodge. For the record, the Hollow was prepared to fight for those seeds rite and socket — but anyone who moves that reverently at speed is doing a kind of liturgy themselves. Take note, Brothers: *that* is how you genuflect at forty metres a second.

Ash!! We replanted the legal pumpkin anyway — Cantor Ilex says paperwork is just gardening for the soul — so EVERYONE won. Except the hauler captain, who lost twice and doesn't know about either time. That's my favourite kind of scoreboard.
